headline: US futures point to a mixed open as tech and AI weakness persists after sharp Asian losses ahead of Fed speakers and key sentiment data
raw_text:
- S&P 500 futures (@ES) fall about 0.5%, Nasdaq 100 futures (@NQ) drop roughly 1.3%, Russell 2000 futures (@ER2) slip about 0.2%, and Dow Jones futures (@YM) are roughly flat in pre-market trade.
- Japan’s Nikkei (@NKD) is down more than 5% and regional Asian markets are on track for their worst week since 2020, contributing to global equities’ longest losing streak since 2023.
- European markets open lower, following overnight Asian selling and extending the global equity downturn.
- Anthropic shares are down about 6% in pre-market trading after their debut, adding to pressure on AI and high-valuation tech names.
- Pre-market single-stock movers are relatively muted, with no major earnings reactions flagged after 4 AM ET.
- Reactions to this morning’s reports from BJ’s Wholesale Club (BJ), Buckle (BKE), Moog (MOG-A), IES Holdings (IESC), and Frontline (FRO) are still developing.
- Fed Governor Waller is scheduled to speak at 8:25 AM ET, kicking off a light US data and events calendar.
- State employment and unemployment data are due at 10:00 AM ET, followed by remarks from Fed Governor Cook at 12:15 PM ET.
- The final University of Michigan consumer sentiment reading is scheduled for 10:00 AM ET.
- Monthly options expiration is on today’s calendar, while oil (@CL) slips about 1% and gold (@GC) trades lower.
